item.title: Noah Kahan Pretends to Call Barack Obama to Revel in Finally Making Ex-Pres’ 2026 Summer Playlist ‘After 15 F–king Years!’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our show, where we bring you the latest music news and trends. Today, we're talking about Noah Kahan's song "Doors" making it onto former President Barack Obama's summer 2026 playlist.
[Music transition]
Host: "Doors" is a track from Kahan's latest album, "The Great Divide", which recently topped the Billboard 200 chart. The song appears alongside other great tunes by artists like Glen Hansard, Doechii & SZA, and Earth, Wind & Fire.
[Clip of Noah Kahan's joke about Obama's playlist]
Host: Kahan playfully acknowledged the honor during a recent show, pretending to have a phone call with Obama and joking about the former president finally putting him on his playlist after 15 years.
[Music transition]
Host: But what's interesting is that "Doors" is a bit of a downer song, with lyrics that touch on self-sabotage and trust issues. It's a departure from some of the other upbeat tracks on Obama's playlist, like Fred Hammond's "I Feel Good" and Chaka Khan's "Ain't Nobody".
[Clip of Noah Kahan's song "Doors"]
Host: Kahan's fans have been having a laugh at the singer's expense, digging up old tweets where he joked about Obama hating his music. But in all seriousness, it's great to see Kahan's song getting recognition from the former president.
[Music transition]
Host: And speaking of politics, Kahan was not amused when the Trump administration used his song "American Cars" in a propaganda video without his consent. He joined a long line of artists who have spoken out against Trump using their music without permission.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our show. We'll be back with more music news and trends soon.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
